machine_model.name: UNIFORM_EXACT_INVARIANT_DESCENT_MACHINE
machine_model.state: S carrying an exact SAT decision semantics for the current instance
requirements: T is deterministic and computable in time polynomial in the original input size N and current polynomially bounded state size
every nonterminal transition is exact: SAT-status is preserved
there is an integer rank rho_F(S) in {0,...,p(N)} for one fixed polynomial p
rho_F(T(S)) <= rho_F(S)-1 on every nonterminal state
all states have size at most q(N) for one fixed polynomial q
terminal states are SAT or UNSAT and are recognizable/verified in polynomial time
all internal work of T and rank/state maintenance is charged

theorem.statement: There exists a uniform exact invariant-descent machine satisfying the frozen requirements for arbitrary 3CNF if and only if P=NP.
forward_direction: The initial rank is at most p(N) and decreases by at least one on every nonterminal transition, so at most p(N) transitions occur.
Each transition and all associated state/rank work cost polynomial time and all states remain polynomial size.
Therefore iterating T reaches an exact SAT/UNSAT terminal in polynomial total time.
Hence 3SAT is in P; since 3SAT is NP-complete, P=NP.
reverse_direction: Assume P=NP, hence 3SAT has a deterministic polynomial-time decider A.
Define T on the initial state to run A(F) and return the corresponding SAT or UNSAT terminal state in one charged transition.
Use rank 1 on the initial nonterminal state and rank 0 on terminal states; state size and transition cost are polynomial.
Thus a machine satisfying the requirements exists.

TRUMP_consequence.claim: The requested object — a polynomially computable exact invariant with guaranteed polynomially bounded strict global descent on every arbitrary 3CNF — is not an easier intermediate milestone. Under the frozen accounting rules its existence is itself equivalent to the final P=NP target.
TRUMP_consequence.admission_rule: Future invariant candidates must therefore be judged as proposed P=NP witnesses: exactness, polynomial transition cost, polynomial state, and universal strict descent must all be proved, not inferred from examples.
what_still_counts_as_progress: discover a concrete exact invariant and prove one or more of the required properties
refute universal descent with an explicit infinite obstruction family
prove a lower bound for a precisely fixed invariant family
prove a composition theorem that combines already exact invariants without hiding exponential search

next_rule: Do not rename the target as a smaller lemma. A new invariant may enter only with a concrete definition and a proof obligation ledger; if universal exact polynomial descent is established, that constitutes a P=NP proof and must undergo independent theorem verification.
